FR-001.title: No audit trail entry for any record the debug seeder creates/updates while running

FR-002.title: Normal user-facing workflows continue to create audit trail entries unchanged

FR-003.title: Audit logging auto-resumes after the seeder finishes, success or error

FR-004.title: Skipping audit writes does not change the seeded data itself

FR-005.title: Seeder remains gated behind its existing opt-in checkbox
tests: manual review — SetupWizard.razor.cs and MauiProgram.cs seeder registration/gating untouched

context: living spec: audit-trail — one AuditTrailEntry per state-changing action, transactionally coupled to the write it documents
living spec: app-host — sample-data seeding is debug-only, opt-in, non-blocking, safe against existing data
area: src/StageFright.Core/Modules/AuditTrail (AuditTrailService.LogAsync is the single choke point ~20 services call through)
constraint: normal (non-seeding) audit logging behavior and its transactional coupling must be unchanged
intent: Stop the debug sample-data seeder from writing audit trail entries, so first-run seeding is fast and the audit trail isn't cluttered with synthetic history
expectations: No new user-facing setting or UI control — behavior change only
No change to what data is seeded, only whether audit entries accompany it
No change to normal (non-seeding) audit logging behavior or its transactional coupling to the write it documents
approach: Add an AsyncLocal-backed AuditTrailSuppressionScope; AuditTrailService.LogAsync no-ops while it is active; DebugDataSeeder.SeedAsync wraps its body in that scope.

T002.did: AuditTrailService.LogAsync no-ops when AuditTrailSuppressionScope.IsSuppressed is true

T003.did: DebugDataSeeder.SeedAsync wraps its body in AuditTrailSuppressionScope.Begin() via using

T004.did: Added AuditTrailSuppressionScope unit tests: default false, begin/dispose, exception-safety via using, flows across await

T005.did: Added LogAsync_DoesNotCallRepository_WhenSuppressed; existing LogAsync_PersistsEntry_WithExpectedFields already covers the not-suppressed case

T006.did: dotnet build: 0 errors; dotnet test: all 1479 tests pass across all 5 projects (6 new suppression tests)

verified.what: full build + test suite after all tasks
verified.result: 0 build errors; 1479/1479 tests pass (6 new), no regressions

decisions.decision: AsyncLocal-backed ambient AuditTrailSuppressionScope, checked once inside AuditTrailService.LogAsync
decisions.why: LogAsync is the single existing choke point ~20 services already call through, so suppression needed zero changes to those callers or the IAuditTrailService interface
decisions.rejected: Threading a suppress-audit bool parameter through IAuditTrailService.LogAsync and every one of its ~20 call sites

decisions.decision: Suppression scope begins/ends inside DebugDataSeeder.SeedAsync itself via using, not at its caller in SetupWizard.razor.cs
decisions.why: keeps the seeder self-contained and guarantees the using/finally safety net applies regardless of how or where SeedAsync is invoked
decisions.rejected: Wrapping the call site in SetupWizard.razor.cs instead

concerns.note: SC-001s zero-writes outcome is verified at the unit level (LogAsync no-ops when suppressed) and by design (SeedAsync wraps its whole body), but a full end-to-end 2-year seed run against a real MAUI app + DB inspection was not performed as part of this implementation, so no wall-clock before/after timing was captured
